title: Watching the dispatcher: what it started, what it is holding, what broke
name: Watching the dispatcher: what it
description:
The dispatcher from the node above runs unattended, which means by default nobody sees it work. Today the only live views are per node — `sober run <node> --watch` follows one agent, `sober logs <node>` reads the last run — and `sober dashboard` serves the board without a queue view. There is no surface that answers "what has it started since I left, and what is it refusing to start".

`runQueue` already returns exactly that shape and it is currently thrown away outside `drain`: `started`, `dispatched` one-per-started, and `held` — each held node with a `why` string already written for a human ("x, y are heading for the same files", "someone has claimed it"). The work is carrying it to a surface, not computing it.

What it shows, per cycle: what started and on which base, what finished and how, what is held and why, and what the concurrency limit is currently refusing. A held node is the important half — an unattended queue that is quietly holding four nodes for a reason nobody reads is worse than one that stopped.

Acceptance: with the dispatcher running, the watch surface shows a node moving from held to started to finished without a restart; a held node shows the same `why` the drain prints today; and closing the watch does not stop the dispatcher. Tests beside the code.

brief.approach:
The dispatcher `sober dispatch` already computes everything this node has to show — `runQueue` returns `started`, `dispatched` and `held`, each held node with a `why` written for a human — and `drain` in `packages/cli/src/queue.ts` already renders all of it. What is missing is that it renders it **once, into the terminal that owns the dispatcher**. Decision `0gma` chose the foreground command, so that terminal is the one you left open and walked away from. There is no second surface that answers "what has it started since I left, and what is it refusing to start".

This node adds that second surface, as a reader. It starts nothing, spends nothing, and closing it does not touch the dispatcher — which is the third acceptance line and the reason it cannot simply be "more output from `sober dispatch`".

## The command

`sober queue` — a new case in `packages/cli/src/index.ts` beside `dispatch`, a new row in the help under **Build**, implemented beside `drain` and `dispatcher` in `packages/cli/src/queue.ts`.

- `sober queue` prints the queue once and exits.
- `sober queue --watch` redraws it on the same `dispatch.pollSeconds` cycle until Ctrl-C.

Per queued node it shows one of: **held** with the `why`, **running** with the run id, **finished** with how it exited. That is the node's "from held to started to finished without a restart" — the watch re-reads the board each cycle, so a node that moved between cycles shows its new state.

It also prints whether a dispatcher is running at all. The ADR 0025 lock on `${paths.lock}-dispatch` is where that already lives — `dispatcher()` holds it for its whole life and reports the holder when a second one starts. Read it the same way and say "a dispatcher is draining this board" or "nothing is draining — start one with `sober dispatch`". Do not add a pidfile; decision `0gma` rejected on-disk liveness and the lock is the mechanism it chose instead.

## One source for `why`

**Do not re-derive the held list in the CLI.** The `why` strings are written inside `runQueue`'s loop in `packages/core/src/queue.ts`, and a second copy in the CLI is two sentences that drift apart on the first edit — the node's own text is explicit that this is carrying, not computing.

Extract the loop body — the claim check and the `overlaps` check — into an exported pure function beside `queued`:

```ts
export const plan = (board: Board, me: string): { start: string[]; held: { id: string; why: string }[] }
```

`runQueue` then calls it and keeps doing exactly what it does now with the result; nothing about its behaviour changes, and its existing tests are the proof. The new command calls the same function with the same board, so a held node reads identically in both places.

`packages/core/src/queue.ts` and `packages/core/src/index.ts` are **not** in this node's declared files. That is deliberate and known — the review will report them as undeclared. The extraction is what keeps the two surfaces honest, and it is smaller than the duplication it avoids.

## What is not in this node

**The dashboard.** `apps/dashboard/src/**` is on the declared list as permission, not as an obligation, and a browser panel needs a server route that is on nobody's list. Every line of the node's acceptance is met in the terminal. Leave `apps/` alone.

**A log file.** The watch reads the board, the runs and the lock — all of which are already on disk and already the truth. A dispatch log would be a fourth copy that goes stale like every file does.

## Tests

`packages/cli/src/queue.test.ts`, beside the existing dispatcher cases, with the same injected-clock shape they already use:

1. A queued node held by an overlap renders the same `why` string `drain` renders — assert the two are equal rather than matching a substring, which is the whole point of the extraction.
2. A board with a held node, then the same board with that node running, then finished, renders three different lines across three cycles of `--watch` without the command restarting.
3. With the dispatch lock free the header says nothing is draining; with it held it names the holder.

And in `packages/core/src/queue.test.ts`, one case that `plan` returns the same split `runQueue` acted on before the extraction.

acceptance.proves: a held node renders the same why the drain prints, and a held, a running and a finished node each read differently across three cycles of the watch without it restarting

acceptance.run: git grep -qE 'plan\(' -- packages/cli/src/queue.ts && pnpm vitest run packages/core/src/queue.test.ts
acceptance.proves: the held list has one author — the CLI calls core plan(), and runQueue still behaves exactly as its own tests describe
liveness is still the ADR 0025 lock and not a file somebody left behind — decision 0gma rejected on-disk liveness

acceptance.run: git grep -qE "case 'queue'" -- packages/cli/src/index.ts && pnpm vitest run --project integration test/integration/cli.test.ts -t 'help'
acceptance.proves: the command is wired and findable in sober --help without reading the source

acceptance.run: test -z "$(git diff --name-only $(git merge-base development HEAD)...HEAD -- apps packages/server)"
acceptance.proves: the dashboard and the server were left alone — a browser panel needs a route nobody declared, and every acceptance line is met in the terminal
the extraction and the new command compile across the monorepo
